Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CTET Paper 2 asks on Symmetry

Questions test line (reflection) symmetry, the number of lines of symmetry of common figures and letters, and rotational symmetry with its order and angle of rotation.

Key facts & formulas to remember

  • A figure has line symmetry if a line divides it into two mirror halves.
  • Lines of symmetry: isosceles triangle 1, equilateral triangle 3, rectangle 2, square 4, circle infinite.
  • A regular polygon of n sides has n lines of symmetry.
  • Rotational symmetry of order n means the figure looks the same n times in one full turn.
  • Angle of rotation = 360° ÷ order (a square has order 4, i.e. 90°).

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Giving a rectangle 4 lines of symmetry (it has only 2).
  • Confusing line symmetry with rotational symmetry.
  • Forgetting that a circle has infinite lines of symmetry.

quiz.title: CTET Symmetry Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten CTET Paper II–pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: A shape has reflection symmetry if it can be divided into two identical halves by a line. Which of the following shapes does NOT have reflection symmetry?
questions.explanation: A general parallelogram (one that is not a rectangle or a rhombus) cannot be folded along any line so that the two halves match — it has no reflection symmetry at all. The equilateral triangle, rectangle, and circle all have at least one line of symmetry.

questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular pentagon have?
questions.explanation: A regular pentagon has 5 lines of symmetry, each passing through one vertex and the midpoint of the opposite side.

questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
questions.explanation: A regular hexagon has 6 lines of symmetry — 3 joining pairs of opposite vertices, and 3 joining the midpoints of opposite sides.

questions.q: Which of the following geometric figures has infinite lines of symmetry?
questions.explanation: A circle can be folded along any diameter and the two halves will always match exactly. Since a circle has infinitely many diameters, it has infinite lines of symmetry.

questions.q: Which of the following capital English letters has reflection symmetry along both a vertical and a horizontal line?
questions.explanation: The letter H has two lines of symmetry — one vertical and one horizontal. F has none, Z has rotational symmetry but no line symmetry, and P has neither.

questions.q: Which of the following letters of the alphabet has reflection symmetry along a vertical line?
questions.explanation: The letter T has a vertical line of symmetry running down its stem. F, G, and S do not have a vertical line of symmetry (S in fact has no line symmetry at all).

questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular octagon have?
questions.explanation: A regular octagon has 8 lines of symmetry, each passing through either a pair of opposite vertices or the midpoints of a pair of opposite sides.

questions.q: Which of the following shapes does NOT have any reflection symmetry?
questions.explanation: A scalene triangle has three sides and three angles that are all different, so no line can divide it into two matching mirror-image halves. Every other shape listed has at least one line of symmetry.

questions.q: Which of the following shapes has 4 lines of symmetry, including both diagonals AND the two lines joining the midpoints of opposite sides?
questions.explanation: A square has all 4 possible lines of symmetry: both diagonals and both lines joining midpoints of opposite sides. A rhombus has only its 2 diagonals as lines of symmetry, a rectangle has only the 2 midpoint-joining lines, and a kite has just 1 line along its main diagonal.

questions.q: When a figure is reflected across its own line of symmetry, what happens to a point that lies exactly on that line?
options: It remains unchanged and maps onto itself.
It moves to the opposite side of the shape.
It maps onto a point parallel to the line.
It moves to the centre of the shape.
questions.explanation: Points lying exactly on the axis of reflection are invariant — their position does not change under the reflection, unlike every other point in the figure.

faq.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
faq.a: Four — two diagonals and the two lines joining the midpoints of opposite sides.

faq.q: What is the order of rotational symmetry?
faq.a: It is the number of times a figure fits onto itself during one complete 360° turn. A square has order 4.
